newsitem.title: USA: Adams says no arms surrender before peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Adams says no arms surrender before peace talks.

text.p: Sinn Fein leader Gerry Adams said on Sunday that the surrender of weapons by the IRA could not be a precondition for his group's participation in peace talks but must be part of the negotiations.

"I think that these talks will get off to the right foot when everybody recognises that we have to meet each other on our own terms," Adams, president of Sinn Fein, the IRA's political arm, said from Belfast on the Fox News Sunday television programme.
"There's no possibility -- and the IRA have made this very clear -- of them surrendering their weapons," he said.
Following the IRA's latest ceasefire declared a week ago, Sinn Fein has been told that it can join peace talks on Northern Ireland in Belfast in September provided the truce was judged to be genuine.

Two pro-British unionist parties walked out of talks in Belfast last week in protest at Anglo-Irish proposals to allow guerrillas to disarm as the talks progress, rather than before or afterwards. The IRA has waged a guerrilla campaign since 1969 to merge the province with Ireland.
Adams also said he hoped that all of the unionist parties would take part in the negotiations.
"I hope the unionists, all of the unionist parties, will sit down and talk acrros the table from the rest of us to try and get agreement on all of these issues," he said.
Britain has sought to assure Sinn Fein that it will not let the issue of "arms decommissioning" hold up negotiations on a lasting settlement to the conflict.
But the British government has yet to find a formula on arms surrender which will satisfy both Sinn Fein and Protestant unionists who want the province to remain British.
